newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Port Arthur massacre defence lawyer resigns - paper.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Port Arthur massacre defence lawyer resigns - paper.

text.p: Australian media on Wednesday reported that the lawyer defending Martin Bryant, who is charged with the country's worst mass murder in modern history, has resigned and another lawyer is considering taking on his case.
Neither lawyer was immediately available for comment.
Bryant on Monday pleaded not guilty to murdering 35 people amongst the ruins of the historic Port Arthur convict jail in the southern island state of Tasmania on April 28.
Bryant, 29, is expected to stand trial on November 19 in the state capital Hobart.
The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper on Wednesday reported that Bryant's lawyer, David Gunson, had resigned.
Gunson, who represented Bryant in his appearance in the Supreme Court of Tasmania on Monday, has refused to comment on the report, according to local newspapers.

But fellow Hobart lawyer John Avery is reportedly considering taking over the case. "I will be clarifying my position in the next 24 hours," Avery was quoted as saying in the Hobart Mercury newspaper on Wednesday.
Bryant's case is due in court again on Friday for a trial date to be set.
On April 28, a sunny Sunday afternoon, a lone gunman walked into the Broad Arrow Cafe at Port Arthur and shot 20 people as they ate their lunch.
Within an hour a further 12 people, including a three-year-old girl, were gunned down either outside the cafe, in their cars, or hiding behind a tree.
Three people were taken hostage and later found dead in the charred remains of the Seascape guest house.
